record.original_question: Does every 2-edge-connected graph with no Petersen minor admit a nowhere-zero 4-flow?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.6 Every 2-edge-connected graph with no Petersen minor has a nowhere-zero 4-flow.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A nowhere-zero 4-flow on a graph $G$ is an orientation of the edges of $G$ together with an assignment of values from $\{1,2,3\}$ to each edge such that, at every vertex, the sum of the values on incoming edges equals the sum of the values on outgoing edges. (Equivalently, $G$ admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow if and only if it admits a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-flow.) A graph $H$ is a minor of $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting edges. The Petersen graph is the 3-regular graph on 10 vertices whose vertices are the 2-element subsets of a 5-element set, with two vertices adjacent iff the corresponding subsets are disjoint. A graph is 2-edge-connected if it is connected and has no bridge.

Prove or disprove: every 2-edge-connected graph that does not contain the Petersen graph as a minor admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Tutte's 4-flow conjecture. It remains open in general. Robertson, Sanders, Seymour, and Thomas announced a proof for the cubic (3-edge-connected, 3-regular) case, but the full conjecture for all 2-edge-connected graphs without a Petersen minor has not been established. Partial results exist for graphs without certain contracted Petersen minors.
